description: A team of four girls from the Kyiv Polytechnic University passionate about technology and its application towards finding solutions of modern challenges . We aim to apply our knowledge and experience toward improving the health and overall well-being of astronauts while they are in space to prevent more complex consequences in future
summary: V.I.T.A is a demo version of a web application designed to support general mental well-being, featuring various tests and the ability to track sleep trends. The website focuses on the importance of tracking exactly this data, as it is critical for productive work in space and for avoiding cognitive biases. By monitoring symptoms and their progression, it becomes possible to detect severe issues early and prevent more serious consequences.
details:
Why it is matter ? What we have considered

Our project, V.I.T.A is an acronym standing for "Vital Indicators Tracking & Analysis". It was developed with a specific purpose: we set out to create a tool that could serve as an aid for monitoring sleep and psychological well-being, while also helping users stick to their habits, as a sport or sleep track reminder.

This web service is designed for a broad audience. It can be useful for individuals over the age of 16 by assisting them in their daily lives, as well as for astronauts currently aboard the International Space Station (ISS). 

The website currently offers psychological tests covering depression, burnout, and interpersonal interactions. We selected precisely this type of test subject matter, inspired by NASA's research on human psychology. In our view, burnout and communication problems can be common problems associated with routine work, limited social interactions, and confined spaces. These tests are based on established scientific instruments. Upon completion, users not only receive their results but also get relevant advice. It is important to note that the tests include a disclaimer stating that they are not a substitute for a professional medical consultation. Nevertheless, we believe they can still be highly valuable for astronauts, first and foremost by allowing them to track changes over the course of their time in space, which can help them obtain necessary guidance and identify concerning symptoms at an early stage. Furthermore, by preserving data, scientists may in the future be able to use information from past tests to better understand how humans adapt to life on space stations. In addition, we have interactive games designed to target cognitive functions, such as memory and reaction speed. We believe that overall well-being and sleep are inextricably linked to mental activity and have a direct impact on it. These are among the most critical attributes an astronaut must possess during a mission, especially before an extravehicular activity(spacewalk), since any issues with reaction within time, concentration, or memory could lead to an error with potentially grave consequences in the space environment. We also have two sleep trackers: a daily one and a weekly one, both of which generate trend data. This information could help scientists study how being in space affects human circadian rhythms and how the body adapts to such conditions. Furthermore, these charts make it possible to stay informed about physical state over an extended period. We also managed to create the foundation for a physical exercise checklist. For astronauts, regular physical exercise is an essential part of living in zero-gravity conditions, as it helps prevent the loss of bone density. But how can one stay motivated to complete tasks that might seem boring at first glance? To address this, we have considered the following factors: our website features a pleasant, light-green visual design, which can have a positive effect on one’s mood. More importantly, we have built a foundation for functional features, such as earning achievements, that can motivate users to keep working through the tests. In addition, we have an interactive pet that not only serves as a reminder of Earth and home but also helps to cheer up. In the future, it could potentially offer advice to astronauts, act as their personal AI agent, or even function like a mini-version of a Tamagotchi to boost motivation for completing tests.

We concluded that adding this specific functionality would enable the site to support multiple users and provide value not only to astronauts, but also directly to people on Earth.

Instruction for usage

On the main page, user can view sleep trends broken down by week, navigate to the "Tests" tab, and see an overall health score based on the data user’s entered. User can also complete a check-up focused on sleep quality over the past week. There are also quotes to lift spirits

On the tests page, there are two tabs containing tests related to psychological health. Оnce user has completed them, they may view and save results, as well as receive an overall analysis and recommendations.

Users also have the option to fill out a sleep diary, recording details such as their bedtime, sleep quality, how they feel, and any issues they may have experienced; over time, this data is used to generate a sleep chart.

There are two games. In the first, the user must click on an icon as quickly as possible when it changes color from red to green. The second game is based on the cognitive function of memory: the user should only click when they see a shape that appeared before the one immediately preceding it.

There is a basis for a checklist where you can mark off the physical exercises you’ve completed on those days.

There is also a separate page for achievements, which serves as an incentive to keep up with daily and weekly tasks.

Benefits of our project 

  1. Flexibility: The project has a wide range of applications, from helping astronauts monitor their health metrics to serving the general public by improving overall well-being, fostering healthy habits, and helping users notice early signs of poor sleep, low mood and burnout 
  2. Speed: Completing the tests takes no more than 5 minutes.
  3. Solutions: After completing the tests, the user receives actionable solutions and advice
  4. Scalability: The project can be expanded in the future, new functionality can be added, and existing features can be improved
  5. Usability: The interface is intuitive, allowing users to figure it out on their own which takes about  5 minutes
  6. Monitoring: Data is stored in a database; users retain access to it and can track their trends over time

The aim of our project 

  1. To help astronauts  monitor and maintain their psychological and physical state far away from earth
  2. People (target audience: 16+) can also actively use our web application to monitor their general well-being 
  3. The website could be extended in future to serve as a platform for developing an application to help people with disorders such as depression and ADHD
  4. To demonstrate the importance of, and the connection between, overall well-being and adherence to a routine

Tool that were used   

  1. The frontend was written in TypeScript
  2. HTML, CSS for interface design
  3. The backend was built using Python
  4. A SQL database was also created with the usage of DataGrip as a primary tool for checking
  5. VS code was the main base for writing the code
  6. AI(Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT) for generating a group emblem, as well as certain aspects of the interface and for debugging code or finding solutions within the code if needed
